A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDiaReward model, dataset and ESDR-Bench. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the new Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, pooling and loss ablations, and a 75-pair human verification study in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds evaluations of specialist and cascade comparators and generalization to unseen synthesis engines.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same architecture, criterion conditioning, pooling choices, Bradley-Terry loss and centering objective. The expanded description of linguistic rewriting matches constraints already present in v1's Appendix B prompts; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends modality evaluation beyond SoulX-Podcast synthesis by testing audio from three unseen engines: OpenAI TTS, CosyVoice 2 and FireRedTTS-2. Existing training sources and colloquialness tasks remain unchanged. Appendix D's audiovisual and singing applications are proposals, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SageLM, SpeechJudge and the AudioReasoner+Whisper+GPT-4o cascade while retaining all previous comparators. New Table 4 evaluates a Wav2Vec2 deepfake detector against SDiaReward, substantially broadening comparison beyond general-purpose audio judges.

E3.justification: The added unseen-engine evaluation reports average rejected-audio reward, Srej, alongside accuracy. Existing splits, micro/macro metrics, training settings and human-study design remain unchanged. v2 specifies the new evaluation only at a high level, without sample counts or detailed sampling and synthesis procedures.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a substantive robustness analysis targeting synthesis-artifact shortcuts through unseen TTS engines, a deepfake-detector control and comparisons of synthetic-audio reward scores. The existing pooling, scale, center-loss and domain-score analyses, including Appendix C, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-annotator, 75-pair human study and identical standard errors in Table 3. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the new evaluations.

E6.justification: v2 adds specialist/cascade results in Table 2 and cross-engine results in Table 4, including SDiaReward-7B accuracies of 98.3%, 95.3% and 90.9% on OpenAI TTS, CosyVoice 2 and FireRedTTS-2. Matched existing results are unchanged. The new CosyVoice 2 Srej is inconsistent: -0.04 in Table 4 versus -0.09 in Section 5.2.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. Neither the expanded discussion nor the new appendix introduces substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about episode-level reward modeling, modality and colloquialness evaluation, leading benchmark accuracy and relative expressiveness beyond synthesis cues. The added experiments support existing claims without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing cascade failures to paralinguistic information loss and interpreting cross-engine rewards as confirming contextual-prosody assessment beyond artifact detection. Section 6 explicitly places DPO/GRPO integration in future work, while new Appendix D extends proposed applicability to audiovisual generation, video speech recognition, singing and agents.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the project-site resource link with a GitHub repository link. v2 identifies components and checkpoints for the added comparisons, including gpt-4o-mini-tts and the Wav2Vec2 detector. Appendix A's training details and Appendix B's construction prompts remain unchanged; detailed OOD reproduction instructions are not added.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands connections to spoken-dialogue benchmarks, adaptive alignment and generative reward modeling, including WavBench, WavAlign and dual-axis reward work. Appendix D adds positioning relative to audiovisual and singing research, while additional references support the new evaluators and synthesis engines.

P1.justification: The title gains the SDiaReward prefix, several explanatory passages receive localized revisions, and the discussion gains a downstream-alignment paragraph and Appendix D. The main section sequence and most existing prose, including the method and prompts, are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains comparator rows and category headings, and a new Table 4 displays OOD accuracy and reward scores. Existing tables and figures reflow, with later tables renumbered. The original figures, plots and prompt displays are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The specialist/cascade comparisons and unseen-engine tests provide useful evidence absent in v1, strengthening the empirical assessment while preserving existing results. However, missing OOD sampling and synthesis details, the overstrong claim that these tests exclude artifact shortcuts, and the CosyVoice 2 table–text discrepancy limit the gain. Overall quality improves, but the central mechanism claim remains insufficiently established.
